strategies.title: BTC 5-minute Up/Down bot run across three wallets
strategies.dossier:
Wallets: GoodFallen 0x0ca4e9d27ff826a109ecbf74754fb66b93f277a6, x-MoneyForWhiskas 0x3048d65321be3497164cdfc2996f94f98a2e7537, dangerously-skip-permissions 0xc53375ff94e96100f2b30a4b5775db35218d69a9 (one operator: thousands of shared transactions, identical price/timing distributions). Known: only BTC 5-minute Up/Down markets; 250k-500k fills a month per wallet; buys both outcomes in most windows at a median pair cost of 1.00-1.01; 33-40% of fills are maker fills (on-chain); its taker buys roughly break even before rebates, its maker fills earn about +3%; about half its profit is the 50% (Obsidian) taker rebate. Best previous match: its passive fills come right after a spot move toward the bought side (signed 2-5 s spot return, strongest at 1 s on Binance), stratified AUC 0.60-0.63, recall 27-40%, lift 1.3-2.3; partly confounded with Polymarket tape momentum; a frozen executable version lost 5-9% on 2,011 unseen windows; the fair-value taker/maker rules did not match. Unknowns: how it prices and sizes its bids, when it cancels, what drives its taker buys (most of its fills), whether it runs inventory-balanced two-sided quoting around a faster fair value, and how the three wallets divide the work. Read: research/verdicts/<wallet>.json, research/wallets/<wallet>/*.json, research/stage_a/updown_btc5m_frozen_rule_extension_binance.json, research/review_2026-10-31/challenge-btc5m-cluster/ (scripts and results).

Reviewer leads (2026-10-31): decode V2 calldata first (a reviewer found a DS maker BUY of 30 at 0.20 signed 9.2 s before its block); the last-60-second settlement-TWAP lock-in (its fills taper at 240-270 s); fixed 30/50/60-share sizes and the salt pattern as fingerprints of a public bot template (one wallet is named dangerously-skip-permissions); its presence AUC is already 0.913 but the activity-only baseline is 0.889, side 66-75%, price within a tick ~49%, PnL correlation 0.31-0.44: those are the real gaps.

strategies.title: Event carry on near-certain outcomes
strategies.dossier:
Wallet: elmcap2 0xed107a85a4585a381e48c7f7ca4144909e7dd2e5. Known: maker bids at 0.92-0.99 on near-certain outcomes held to resolution (98% maker fills by count); about $5.7M peak capital at risk; the last month's profit is essentially the October 2026 FOMC book (+$258k on $4.39M bought within ~5 days of the statement); 'nothing happens by the deadline' NO positions at 0.99+; parks idle cash as complete sets in a no-trade market for holding yield. Previous reviewer rules: FOMC consensus carry AUC 0.785 (recall 26%, precision 49%), deadline-NO carry AUC 0.854 (recall 53%, precision 5.6%); neither profitable at p<0.05. It fails the 10%/month return-on-capital criterion regardless, but the goal here is to decipher its selection, entry timing, pricing and sizing as accurately as possible. Holdout = events resolving on or after 2026-10-23. Read: research/verdicts/0xed107a85a4585a381e48c7f7ca4144909e7dd2e5.json, research/wallets/0xed107a85a4585a381e48c7f7ca4144909e7dd2e5/, research/review_2026-10-31/challenge-carry-elmcap2/.

Reviewer leads (2026-10-31): holding rewards (Gamma holdingRewardsEnabled) as the reason for its parking and market selection; CME FedWatch and fed funds futures (A6b) and Kalshi FOMC prices (A4b) for its FOMC book.

strategies.title: In-play US sports taker reacting to game events
strategies.dossier:
Wallet: justaluckydude 0xbca08c1bc204a34f2fddbe47b438b9bd42ac9705. Known: 100% taker fills, nearly all after game start, US sports (college football, NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL) moneylines, spreads and totals; its fills spike 4x in the 5 s after ESPN scoring plays; within 10 s windows (5 s ESPN delay) 95% of its buys favour the scoring side vs 60% for other takers, but only ~11% of its buys fall in those windows; a reviewer rule reacting to any ESPN win-probability swing covered 36% of buys (AUC 0.648); no rule was significantly profitable with a realistic delay; profit concentrated in college football and MLB; profit decaying. Unknowns: what explains the other ~64% of its buys (pre-play anticipation? line moves on related markets? other data feeds such as faster score sources, injury news, drive/possession state, ESPN win probability levels), how it chooses line and price, sizing. Read: research/verdicts/0xbca08c1bc204a34f2fddbe47b438b9bd42ac9705.json, research/wallets/0xbca08c1bc204a34f2fddbe47b438b9bd42ac9705/, research/review_2026-10-31/challenge-inplay-taker-justaluckydude/.

Reviewer leads (2026-10-31): a hazard model of its buys given drive and field position (football) or base-out state (baseball), i.e. anticipating scores rather than reacting; MLB statsapi pitch-level and NHL api-web play-by-play timestamps against its order signing times.

strategies.title: Crypto Up/Down volume trader whose profit is the taker rebate
strategies.dossier:
Wallet: 0xb55fa1296e6ec55d0ce53d93b9237389f11764d4. Known: about 467k fills in 30 days across BTC/ETH/SOL 5m, 15m, hourly and 4h Up/Down windows (BTC 15m and hourly/daily are its largest families); 30% maker fills on-chain; trading loses about $48.6k a month after fees (pre-fee +$108k); profit is a Diamond-tier (44%) taker rebate plus a one-off $25k level-up bonus; no public rule matched its taker or maker decisions (latency taker, directional maker, spot-reactive maker, tape-anchored maker, late-favourite taker, hourly spot taker all failed). The goal is to decipher its actual trading logic (which windows, sides, prices, timing, sizes; how it manages volume for the rebate) as accurately as possible even though it is unprofitable before rebates. Read: research/verdicts/0xb55fa1296e6ec55d0ce53d93b9237389f11764d4.json, research/wallets/0xb55fa1296e6ec55d0ce53d93b9237389f11764d4/, research/review_2026-10-31/challenge-rebate-farmer/.

Reviewer leads (2026-10-31): self-matching or circular volume with its own or related wallets, referral income (C7); the maker rebate pool share by market (B9); fingerprints of its order software (C8).

strategies.title: Directional crypto Up/Down maker run across three wallets
strategies.dossier:
Wallets: bosona 0xc2ad03f79ca3f3c17d8c7de2612ce0c89b7d40ed, almach 0x3725d52f3c252e8374999cc8617292ea2608ad88, mo-money 0x32ed2e546b187ca15e2841edc82b22c713cf8ec3 (one operator: about 6,500-6,900 shared transactions per pair, ~80% of markets shared). Known: 89-94% maker fills; BTC 5m (~55%) and 15m (~28%) Up/Down plus hourly, 4h and some ETH/SOL; buys only one side in more than half of its windows; its profit is the directional residual (win rate ~57-58%), the locked pair spread is about zero or negative; little rebate dependence (Gold 18%); its own maker fills earn +3% to +6% in held-out windows while every public-data maker built from the same data (spot fair value, spot-reactive, tape-anchored, fixed ladders, buy-the-dip) loses or is insignificant; only weak associations (stratified AUC 0.53-0.59, recall 2-47%, lift 1.1-2.3). Unknowns: how it decides which side to bid, at what price and size, when it cancels, whether it uses a faster or different reference price (Binance aggTrades, Coinbase, Chainlink), queue priority, how the three wallets split the work. Read: research/verdicts/<wallet>.json, research/wallets/<wallet>/*.json, research/stage_a/updown_btc5m_frozen_rule_extension_binance.json, research/stage_a/updown_btc5m_maker_baselines.json, research/review_2026-10-31/challenge-crypto-maker-cluster/.

Reviewer leads (2026-10-31): liquidity-reward eligibility (BTC 5m rewardsMinSize 50 and rewardsMaxSpread 4.5; almost all of its holdout profit is in fills over 40 shares); operational events (matching-engine restarts with 2-minute post-only mode, tick changes, pauses) as the cause of its 19-97% daily activity; V2 calldata signing times to measure its requote speed directly against Binance, the settlement TWAP and the recorded books.
strategies.prior_diagnosis: Exam round 1 (the whole of lots h1 and h2, 2026-10-23..31, now development data: 2,304 BTC 5m windows, 36,244 cluster maker fills) judged match partial: presence AUC 0.700 vs 0.681 for market activity alone (+0.019), side accuracy 0.655 vs 0.600, price within one tick 0.688, selection AUC 0.681 with recall 32% at lift 2.6, per-window PnL correlation 0.29; every metric fell from VALIDATE except price. The executable rule lost 12.8% under strict fills on every day, while the wallets' own BTC 5m maker fills earned +3.95% (p=0.005). The examiner's reading: the cluster is a top-of-book liquidity provider on the 0.01 grid that requotes or cancels faster than other makers after Binance moves (its fill rate rises 1.6x after sharp moves vs 3x for other makers), with an operator schedule of which windows to trade (active share 19-97% by day) that the rule never decoded; almost all profit is in fills > 40 shares and in mid-window (30-120 s) fills. Undecoded: selection of windows, quote placement and cancel timing, size. These are now targets, not walls: try calldata order reconstruction (original size, expiration, signer), the live lab (book at its decision times), the settlement feed, sibling wallets and bot versions. Full text: EXAM_r1.md and results/exam_r1.json.

strategies.title: In-play multi-sport taker (soccer goals, quiet books)
strategies.dossier:
Wallet: 0xdbdd45150249e229eb4ca8aa48a30dca21faa5de. Known: 100% taker fills, median fill about $11, nearly all after game start; trades soccer (where it makes its money: +$59.8k on $1.32M outside US leagues), tennis, US sports (where it loses), CS2 and Dota 2; in soccer totals 26% of its buys fall within 60 s after an ESPN goal wall clock (other takers 10%), 96% of those are Over; it trades disproportionately when the book has been quiet for 10 s or more; spreads lagging the moneyline match its US trades; bought shares win more often than their price at 0.65-0.85; no reviewer rule (seven tried) was profitable on fresh games. Unknowns: its selection of line and price after goals, what it does in tennis and esports, whether it reacts to faster score feeds or to cross-market moves, sizing. Read: research/verdicts/0xdbdd45150249e229eb4ca8aa48a30dca21faa5de.json, research/wallets/0xdbdd45150249e229eb4ca8aa48a30dca21faa5de/, research/review_2026-10-31/challenge-inplay-taker-0xdbdd/.

Reviewer leads (2026-10-31): the strong form of copy trading (same token and side, a fixed size ratio, a 0-30 s lag; its median fill is $11); stale-quote sniping against a fair value made consistent across the same event's markets (moneyline, draw, totals ladder); the Polymarket sports websocket's soccer minutes and scores.

strategies.title: Large in-play two-sided market maker (soccer, tennis, CS2, US football)
strategies.dossier:
Wallet: RN1 0x2005d16a84ceefa912d4e380cd32e7ff827875ea. Known: about 249k fills and $65M a month; 92% maker fills; resting bids on both sides of live markets, soccer ~45% of volume, tennis and esports ~40%; complete pairs bought at a median combined 0.982 lock +$964k a month while the unmatched residual loses $319k; around ESPN scoring plays only 1.4% of its passive fills land in the first 5 s (all makers 4.9%), and after soccer goals it is off the book before the first public price jump; best families WTA, CFB, UCL, CS2, La Liga, ATP; public-data makers lose 5-19% in its markets, including its best families. Unknowns: its quote placement (spread, levels, sizes), requote and cancel timing, inventory rules, which signals make it withdraw, and why its pair cost is below 1. On-chain order reconstruction (orderHash) should be very informative here. Read: research/verdicts/0x2005d16a84ceefa912d4e380cd32e7ff827875ea.json, research/wallets/0x2005d16a84ceefa912d4e380cd32e7ff827875ea/, research/review_2026-10-31/challenge-inplay-maker-RN1/.

Reviewer leads (2026-10-31): Combos/RFQ flow (Gamma rfqEnabled) as a hedge or a source of its two-sided quoting; the Polymarket sports websocket's latency against ESPN and against its V2 order signing times (it is off the book before the first public price jump after goals).

strategies.title: CS2 in-play market maker (switched from taker mid-October)
strategies.dossier:
Wallet: TommyLeePeeca 0x0063b23cdeb43166d6c0246c05baaf9b9bd72dd2. Known: 98% CS2 (some Dota 2); until 15 October a taker (losing before rebates), from 16-17 October a two-sided maker: in 17-29 October it made $43.7k, every day positive, pair cost about 0.98; its maker fingerprint is keeping bids pegged while the price falls where other makers pull (AUC 0.54, lift 1.2); public-data makers lose 5-9% in the same matches. Development data for the maker regime is 16-23 October (the holdout starts 23 October); you may also study the earlier taker regime. Unknowns: its quote placement and sizing, requote/cancel timing around rounds, inventory balancing, which signals (round results, economy, map state from public CS2 data such as bo3.gg or HLTV if reachable) it uses.
